snippet.title: When Do You See the Heartbeat After IVF? First Ultrasound Explained
snippet.description:
When can you see the heartbeat at the first ultrasound after IVF, and what if there's no cardiac activity yet? Dr Senai Aksoy, Associate Professor of Reproductive Medicine, explains what the doctor looks for, week by week.

In short: cardiac activity is usually visible at around 6 weeks of pregnancy. Too early is not necessarily a bad sign: a follow-up scan at least a week later is often planned before drawing any conclusion.

Inside: how weeks of pregnancy are counted after an embryo transfer, what a transvaginal scan shows and when, the criteria for a follow-up scan, what the studies say about pregnancies that continue, ectopic pregnancy, and the warning signs that should never wait for your next appointment.

CHAPTERS
00:00 Short answer: the heartbeat at around 6 weeks
01:20 What if it's a bit early?
01:36 Which "first ultrasound"?
01:53 The mystery of the weeks
02:56 With IVF: the exact date, converted
03:18 Two clocks, one uterus
03:49 What should we see, and when?
04:14 Transvaginal scan landmarks
05:17 What if there's no cardiac activity yet?
05:43 NICE NG126 guidance (UK)
06:04 US study, October 2025
07:06 How many pregnancies continue?
08:10 Safety: ectopic pregnancy
09:02 Signs that should never wait
09:41 Support medications and progesterone
10:02 My clinical opinion: a scan at 5 weeks?
10:37 To answer the question from the start
11:10 Three questions for your appointment

3 QUESTIONS FOR YOUR APPOINTMENT
1. Exactly how many weeks pregnant will I be on the day of the scan, and what do you expect to see?
2. If not everything is visible yet, when do we do the follow-up scan, and who will give me the results?
3. Until what exact date should I keep taking my medications, and who decides when to stop?

SOURCES CITED IN THE VIDEO
NICE NG126: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng126 · Mortimer et al., AJOG 2025 · Spandorfer, Fertil Steril 2004 · Yi et al., Reprod Biol Endocrinol 2016 · Doubilet, NEJM 2013 · Bree, AJR 1989

Severe one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, fainting or heavy bleeding: go to the emergency department or call your local emergency number. Do not wait for your next appointment.

Website: https://www.draksoyivf.com

Your individual circumstances require assessment by a qualified clinician. Do not start, stop or change any prescribed treatment based on this video without consulting your doctor.

LANGUAGE AND PRODUCTION
This is an English-dubbed version of Dr Aksoy's original French educational video, using an AI voice based on Dr Aksoy's own voice. Lip movements were not altered. Supporting footage is illustrative.
